rows.subtype: Always and never after one event [Actor]
rows.description: A child picked last once says nobody ever chooses them and they never win; a single event is stretched into a rule for life.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager refused by one peer group decides that no one will ever accept them; the sample of one is used as if it were the whole world.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who thinks they always freeze in exams lists times they did not and what was different; counter-examples loosen the rule and reveal what to work on.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: One bad boss means all workplaces [Actor]
rows.description: An adult with a difficult first job decides that all workplaces are toxic and stops trying; the experience is real but the conclusion outruns the evidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager who received nine praises and one criticism on a project can only recall the criticism; the mind's spotlight lands on what hurt and dims the rest.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Only the negatives in a review [Actor]
rows.description: A student goes over a feedback form and fixes on a single frowning comment and forgets the many good ones; the filter makes success feel like failure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team lead sees an employee leave a good review meeting convinced they were criticised because of one line; the lead reads the whole page aloud and asks what else it says.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult deliberately lists three things that went well next to the one that did not before deciding what to do; balanced attention corrects bias and does not deny the criticism.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager who is praised for a good drawing says it was just luck and anyone can do it; good news is explained away so the negative self-view stays untouched.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who topped a paper says the exam was easy so it means nothing; every success is reclassified as a fluke while every failure is treated as proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
